questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live in another country for a period to see if it was something for me and i thought doing a semester abroad could help facilitate that :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Medium. The host- and sendning university staff were great at helping with the process of signing up to the different classes, but at the host university a lot of the processes of how to sign up for exams, guest lectures and so on could have been comunicated better

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recived information regarding the sign-up process for classes through an email from the host uni

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. My biggest recomendation to anyone planniung to study in milan is to sign up for the campus housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: DO NOT BOOK accomendation through AIRBNB. Landlords in milan are horrible. When i arrived to my apartment in milan there was black mold all over the walls throughout the apartment and the landlord refused to help solve the issue.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was troubled by a lot of the classes that i signed up for had changed curriculum, focus or even to a totally different class with differnt contents after the classes had started. So while the registration process was not the most diffiult, having to readjust and email the professors regarding the changes was pretty annoying.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: none. emailing the professors was of absolutely no help and proved to be more of a nuisance that anything else :)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: okay succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reconsider going to milan. Theres a lot of other great places to do a semester of exchange and milan is certainly not one of them :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very unsatisfied

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses af the host uni was very low. With no reading or class attendance, youre still guarenteed to pass any exam

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: very different. all of the classes at the host uni consisted of a professor, barely speaking english, talking semi-coherent for almost 2 hours. there was no discussion of the topics or anything close

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: globalisation and regionlisation in international security, international economic law, comparative political economy and the wellfare state, global challenges to democracy

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *

questions.answer: probaly quite a few, but i never looked into it

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: dont know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go travel around as much as you possibly can. Get out of milan and try to visit a lot of the smaller cities nearby

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: hard. While the milanese culture was quite easy to adjust to, the culture at uni was much more difficult to adjust to. The professors showed up late almost every time - even for exams. the students at uni smoked weed in the courtyard of the uni, resulting in a particularly unpleasant smell in the lecture halls....

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: try to go to a lot of the esn events at the start of the semester. The events are all pretty shitty, but they're a worthwhile investment to meet other people whom are studying abroad

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As detailed above, the professors constantly showing up late for exams, the strict social hierachy at universities in italy and the near constant smell of weed at university

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the cheap flights out of italy

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be VERY carefull who you choose to live with, dont go to milan to study and if you do, please be careful to walk around alone at night - especially as a woman

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: se above text

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting new friends from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: apart from a shitty housing situation with a poor selection of roomates, i found it the hardest to adjust to the much lower academic level at host uni

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
